title: POC weekly sync - Meridian Retail pilot - final results & closeout
summary: Weekly POC closeout: reviewed final benchmark numbers for Meridian Retail intent-classification and autocomplete workloads, discussed tuning that enabled cost/latency targets, aligned on success criteria and business case, agreed next steps for exec review and procurement path for Dedicated capacity or Hosted with strong SLA.
topics: tuning applied: batching, quantization, KV/prefix caching
next steps: pricing, security docs, executive review
action_items: Sofia Patel - Send consolidated benchmark spreadsheet + short 1-pager ROI summary - 2025-09-10
Diego Ramos - Export run-level logs and p95 latency traces for 09/03-09/07 and upload to shared folder - 2025-09-09
Laura Chen - Confirm final success criteria thresholds from product leadership (latency, accuracy, cost targets) - 2025-09-12
Ellen Park - Share procurement timeline and required PO info - 2025-09-15
next_steps: Redwood to send final benchmark + pricing options (hosted vs dedicated) and recommended config
Customer to schedule 30m exec review with CTO and Head of Ops next week
Agree final pilot acceptance criteria in writing after exec review
Procurement to review quote and confirm PO path or dedicated contract request
transcript: 00:00:01 Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick check — can you all hear me?
00:00:05 Laura: Yep can hear you, Laura here. Sorry running late, just joined.
00:00:12 Tom: Tom from product, hi all.
00:00:18 Diego: Diego from Redwood, I'll kick off the bench review slides, share screen in a sec.
00:00:32 Sofia: Objective today is to review the final numbers from the pilot, confirm if we hit success criteria and agree next steps for procurement and exec sign off.

00:01:05 Diego: Alright slide one — we ran two workloads: intent classification at 1k qps sim and autocomplete/assist at a lower qps, mixed sequences. Baseline hosted model (v1.3) vs tuned quantized v1.3-q4 and a dedicated variant with larger batch sizing.
00:01:46 Laura: Quick question, the qps is synthetic right? It matches our peak but not typical, correct?
00:01:55 Diego: Correct, peak sims to stress latency/kv cache behavior — we also ran production trace replay which is in the spreadsheet.

00:02:30 Diego: Key numbers: intent classification p50 ~ 85ms on dedicated, p95 ~ 210ms; hosted avg p50 120ms p95 430ms. For autocomplete p50 140ms p95 360ms on tuned hosted. Cost per 1M input tokens dropped ~28% after quantization + prefix caching.
00:03:12 Tom: That p95 gap on hosted worries me at peak — is that due to batching or cold-starts?

00:03:20 Diego: Mostly KV cache misses and tail queuing at burst windows; tuning batch size from 1 to 8 and enabling prefix caching brought p95 down ~120ms in the critical window. Also we saw benefits from adaptive batching in the dedicated pool.
00:04:05 Laura: What about accuracy drift with quantization? We need to make sure NPS isn't impacted for the recommender prompts.
00:04:18 Diego: We ran A/B on 3k test prompts — delta in top-1 classification was 0.4% absolute which is within your guardrail of 1%. Autocomplete hallucination rate unchanged in our sampled checks.
00:05:00 Tom: Ok that's acceptable, but let's capture that as acceptance criteria explicitly.
00:05:12 Sofia: Noted — Laura can you confirm that's acceptable?
00:05:18 Laura: Yes 0.4% delta is ok, as long as we have the rollout plan to monitor drift live and rollback quickly.
00:05:40 Diego: We added monitoring hooks in the runbook — realtime error and quality dashboards, and automatic rollback on threshold breach. See the runbook link we shared.

00:06:15 Rohit: From infra side we tested VPC peering with dedicated even though this was a hosted pilot; latency overhead in our region was ~12ms extra for the round trip but stable. Any encryption concerns?
00:06:30 Diego: All traffic can be TLS 1.3 and customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments; for Dedicated we provide HSM/KMS integration too. We included TLS details in security docs.
00:07:05 Ellen: Procurement — rough numbers? We need to compare hosted monthly run-rate vs committed dedicated price.

00:07:18 Sofia: We'll send the pricing sheet. For your usage profile we estimated hosted at $X/month and dedicated reserved at a 20-30% lower unit cost depending on commit level. We put detailed numbers in the quote PDF.
00:07:55 Tom: Can you remind us what the success criteria list is? I want to ensure execs see it in the review.

00:08:05 Sofia: Sure it's: 1) p95 latency under 250ms for intent workload; 2) less than 1% model quality regression on key intents; 3) projected TCO reduction of at least 15% vs current prod path; 4) operational runbook and SRE playbook accepted.
00:08:32 Laura: Do we want p50 goals too?
00:08:36 Diego: We proposed p50 under 100ms for intent; it's in the spreadsheet.
00:09:10 Laura: Sounds good — if those are met I'll sign off to push to exec review.
00:09:25 Sofia: Next up the business case — Diego walk through the ROI slide.

00:09:33 Diego: With the tuning we get 28% token cost reduction and 18% better throughput on dedicated. Assuming current monthly token volume, modeled savings net of infra is about 22% annualized which hits your 15% TCO target. We included conservative and aggressive scenarios in the workbook.
00:10:10 Tom: That's promising. Any hidden ops costs we missed? Support/SLA tiers?

00:10:18 Sofia: Dedicated includes a support SLA option; higher SLAs have a fixed monthly premium. We'll mark those in the quote. Also note integration engineering effort estimated at ~2-3 weeks for full rollout (network, IAM, observability).
00:10:40 Ellen: Procurement will need the final quote + SOW to process a PO. If you can add line items for support tiers that's helpful.
00:10:50 Sofia: Will do. We'll send line-itemized quote and sample SOW.
00:11:12 Laura: Operational question — what's our rollback plan if accuracy drifts after rollout?
00:11:20 Diego: Quick rollback to previous model variant + cache flush, and we have canary rollout with A/B for 10% then 50% then full. Playbook in runbook.
00:11:50 Tom: Good. Anything else on risks?
00:11:58 Rohit: From SRE, we want automated alerting to PagerDuty on p95 breaches and quota exhaustion — can integrate with your tracing hooks?
00:12:10 Diego: Yep we have tracing hooks and alert webhooks; we'll provide sample Grafana dashboards and Prometheus exporters for your stack.

00:12:40 Sofia: Recap — we need to get the final benchmark spreadsheet, pricing options, security pack, and runbook to you by Wednesday. Laura will confirm success criteria in writing. Customer schedules an exec review next week. Procurement to confirm PO path and timeline.
00:12:58 Laura: I'll get criteria to you by Friday, and I'll book the exec slot for next Tue/Wed.
00:13:10 Ellen: Procurement will try to have initial feedback by 9/15, that's our internal target.
00:13:25 Sofia: Perfect. Any final questions?
00:13:30 Tom: One thing — does Redwood offer a trial dedicated month or a small reserved node we can test live?
00:13:40 Diego: We can do a limited reserved node pilot for 30 days under a short-term contract, yes — Diego will follow up with the test details.
00:13:55 Sofia: Great. Thanks everyone — will follow up with artifacts and next steps.
00:14:02 Laura: Thanks all.
00:14:05 Meeting end
